fact_claims.verbatim: Northwind’s company-wide thermal incident rate last year was 8.6 per 100,000 installed units
the Hearth 10 model rate was 6.4 per 100,000
Halcyon’s company-wide thermal incident rate last year was 8.1 per 100,000 installed units
the Ember 8 model rate was 9.9 per 100,000
Four thermal incidents last year were not reported to any regulator.
Northwind had 3 thermal incidents last year that were not reported to any regulator.

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers shall report to the relevant regulator any thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or material property damage within 24 hours of learning of it, with a written incident report within 10 calendar days. Suspected serious or fatal incidents must be reported immediately and no later than 4 hours.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C before sale and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-accepted protocol and representative samples. The maximum allowed failure rate is 5%.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units placed on the market from 24 months after adoption shall support secure remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear customer instructions. For units already installed on the adoption date, manufacturers shall provide compatible retrofit capability or an equivalent safe mitigation within 6 years, prioritizing units with known safety concerns.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units placed on the market from 36 months after adoption shall include built-in fire suppression meeting applicable safety requirements.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall promptly notify the regulator and affected customers and cooperate in a regulator-supervised recall assessment. The regulator shall require a recall when the threshold is exceeded, unless it determines that a time-bound corrective action provides an equally protective remedy; an equivalent serious risk independently warrants a recall.

document.section_notes: S1 sets strict reporting timelines (4h serious, 24h other, 5d customer notice) and broad incident scope, but does not explicitly require reporting during an ongoing investigation. S2 keeps the 55°C test and 5% limit with a time-bound corrective-action path and regulator-determined sales restrictions, gives numeric results to purchasers but not the public. S3 requires new-unit shut-off from 24 months and installed-unit retrofit/equivalent within 6 years, with no feasibility escape; the 24-month new-unit deadline is outside the acceptable range. S4 requires built-in suppression from 36 months, which is acceptable. S5 retains the 8-per-100k recall trigger but allows a bounded corrective action instead of recall, with only prompt notice language and no explicit serious-injury recall clause.
